changes: The VPN key in the status bar while a tunnel is up.
Always on: one WireGuard or AmneziaWG profile and one Tailscale profile together.
Your WireGuard and AmneziaWG tunnels on BlackBerry 10, IPv4 and IPv6: add a profile from a .conf file, a QR code or pasted text - or open a .conf "in Tunnel" from a mail or the file manager.
An AmneziaVPN key works too: its text (vpn://...), a .vpn file or the QR codes AmneziaVPN shows for it.

Tailscale: your tailnet's devices - a NAS behind any router too - by name (MagicDNS) or by their 100.x addresses, logged in by a link - opened on a computer or another phone from its QR code - or with an auth key; the traffic goes directly - in the same network (a NAS at home over Wi-Fi) and through the internet when the routers on both sides let it - otherwise through Tailscale's relays, inside a full tunnel such as WARP too.
The connections list: a switch per profile, its state in words, several tunnels at once - a split one beside the one that takes all traffic.
A profile's page: its state and what it means, the traffic and the last handshake, its public key, addresses, DNS, server and routes.
A tunnel's DNS servers serve the whole phone while it is up: names are looked up through the tunnel, not past it.
Always on: a profile that comes up when the phone boots and stays up across network changes.
Notifications from the background service: a lost connection, a tunnel service that does not answer, and on request a quiet mark in the Hub while a tunnel is up.
Diagnostics: the tunnel service's log, a detailed one for a while when you ask (it turns itself off); all the logs - its start at boot included - shared in one tap.
An update of Tunnel takes effect after a restart of the phone - the app says when one is needed.
How to start: a guide on the first start and in the app menu - the tunnel service and its start at boot, which the app sets up by itself, whether the service answers, and your first profile.
